PZwiki - Admin commands (Build 42 command list zomboid_rcon tracks)

notes: Commands are sent over RCON without a leading slash; the slash seen in wiki and blog write-ups is the in-game admin-chat form. zomboid_rcon builds exactly these words - players, kickuser, banuser, unbanuser, servermsg, showoptions - and SuperCraft, ScalaCube and XGamingServer independently list the same syntax with the username quoted and -r "reason" appended. Project Zomboid moderates by USERNAME, not Steam ID: kickuser/banuser/unbanuser take the account name. There are separate banid/unbanid commands that take a Steam ID, and banuser also accepts -ip (ban the IP) and, on Build 42, -s (also ban the Steam ID); neither extra flag is used in the templates here because both widen the ban beyond what a plain ban button should do. Bans have no duration - the game has no timed ban - so ban carries no {duration}. showoptions is used as info because it is the only command that reports current server state; there is no serverinfo command. No motd command exists: the welcome message is the ServerWelcomeMessage .ini option, changeable with changeoption plus reloadoptions rather than a broadcast-style command. CAUTION on servermsg: zomboid_rcon replaces spaces with underscores before sending 'for compatibility', while SuperCraft, ScalaCube and XGamingServer all show a quoted multi-word message working; the quoted form is recorded here as the majority reading, and a caller seeing one-word-only output should fall back to underscores. UNCORROBORATED: playerParse was not confirmed against a captured 'players' response by any source reached - every guide describes the command without showing output. It is written to be tolerant: the header line ('Players connected (n):') and anything else not starting with '-' is skipped, and each remaining '-name' line yields the name as both display name and id. SuperCraft says Build 42 also prints an access level per player, which would break the whole-line capture; treat this block as the first thing to check on a live server. No banList block is recorded: Project Zomboid keeps bans inside the SQLite world database (db/<servername>.db), not in a line-oriented text file, so there is nothing a lineIdPattern could read - unbanuser and unbanid are the supported route. One hosting blog (WinterNode) publishes '/kick PlayerName' and '/banuser PlayerName true'; Project Zomboid has no 'kick' command and banuser takes no trailing boolean, so that source was discarded.
